paper_title: Clustering Permutations Under the Ulam Metric: A Parameterized Complexity Study
classifications: Theory of computation → Parameterized complexity and exact algorithms
Mathematics of computing → Permutations and combinations
statement: It is known [18] that Closest String cannot be solved in 2o(d log d) · (nm)O(1) time unless the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH) fails (we refer to [18] for the formal definition of ETH). Then the Polynomial Parameter Transformation from Theorem 3 implies the same computational lower bound for Ulam Metric 1-Center. Is it possible to solve Ulam Metric 1-Center for k = 1 in dO(d) · (nm)O(1) time similarly to Closest String?
context: We initiated the study of the parameterized complexity of the Ulam Metric k-Center and Ulam Metric k-Median problems. Prior to our work, even the parameterized complexity for the case k = 1 with parameter d was unknown for these problems. It is known [18] that Closest String cannot be solved in 2o(d log d) · (nm)O(1) time unless the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH) fails (we refer to [18] for the formal definition of ETH). Then the Polynomial Parameter Transformation from Theorem 3 implies the same computational lower bound for Ulam Metric 1-Center. Is it possible to solve Ulam Metric 1-Center for k = 1 in dO(d) · (nm)O(1) time similarly to Closest String? For Ulam Metric k-Median, it is shown that the problem is W[1]-hard when parameterized by d but is in XP under the same parameterization. Furthermore, the problem admits a polynomial kernel for the parameterization by both k and d. The latter result together with an XP-algorithm implies that Ulam Metric k-Median can be solved in (kd)O(d) · (mn)O(1) time. Is it possible to improve this running time? Similarly to Ulam Metric k-Center, we find that this question is interesting even for k = 1. Is there a single-exponential (or even subexponential) in d algorithm?
